## Overview

**This is a comparator, not the model of record.** It is [LRPLF01](../lrp-rli-lf-001/index.qmd) restricted to the two waves at which randomisation alone separates the arms — the pre-randomisation baseline t1 and the end of the randomised period t2 (#584 decision 3). Same model, same adjustment set, same estimand.

In the four-wave fit the post-crossover t3/t4 likelihood reaches the reported t2 change through parameters the waves share: the balance term `arm_gap_t1` the changes are measured from, the child random intercept, the dispersion, and the single time-invariant `group × ability` term. Across the level suite the posterior correlation between `arm_gap_t1` and `d_grp_time[t2]` runs from −0.07 to −0.44, so the contrast is randomisation-anchored but also longitudinal-model-dependent. Here there is nothing to borrow, and the difference between the two fits is the size of that dependence.

Read the four-wave report for the levels view across all four timepoints — showing them on one scale is that model's purpose, and this restriction gives it up.

LRPLF201 is a **level-factors** model for word reading (`ewrswr`): what is associated
with the word-reading score *level* at the two included timepoints (t1 and t2),
modelled on the logit scale with a Beta-Binomial likelihood and a child random
intercept. Unlike the gain model it is **not autoregressive** — there is no own
baseline; per-timepoint intercepts absorb the maturation trend.

_Causal labelling + the level-model crossover caveat._ Under the revised study DAG (`dag/dag-language-reading.dagitty`, revised 2026-07-10)
every non-randomised coefficient is an **adjusted association** confounded by latent
general ability (the child random intercept is
only a partial, shrunken stand-in for between-child heterogeneity, not a control for
that latent general ability) — "associated with", never "drives". **Crucially,
the group effect is modelled as `group × time` — a per-timepoint group coefficient,
read as trajectory divergence — because after t2 the waitlist crosses over: the
group difference across the four timepoints is *not* a clean ITT contrast.** This
comparator fits only the two waves where it is: the arm coefficient is the
covariate-adjusted gap at t1 (`arm_gap_t1`, a pre-randomisation *balance* quantity,
never an effect) plus the change in that gap at t2 (`d_grp_time[t2]`; #552), which
is the clean randomised contrast, labelled *causal* in the table below. The
post-crossover waves are not in this fit, so there are no t3/t4 schedule contrasts
to read — and nothing for the t2 change to borrow from them. SES
is excluded (non-DAG / redundant).

**DAG factor set:** group $\times$ time · age (per timepoint) · cognitive ability
(block design) $\times$ time · group $\times$ ability · child random intercept.

## Model

$$
\operatorname{logit}\mu_{i,t} = \alpha + \alpha_{\text{time}[t]}
  + b_{\text{grp}[t]}\,\text{group}_i
  + \gamma_A A_{\text{std},t}
  + g_{\text{ability}[t]}\,z(\text{blocks})
  + \gamma_{\text{grp\_ability}}\,\text{group}_i\,z(\text{blocks})
  + u_{\text{child}[i]},
$$

with $W_t \sim \operatorname{BetaBinomial}(N, \mu\kappa, (1-\mu)\kappa)$, $N = 79$.
The per-timepoint group ($b_{\text{grp}[t]}$) and ability ($g_{\text{ability}[t]}$)
coefficients are the `group × time` and `ability × time` interactions; the clean
randomised contrast is the change in $b_{\text{grp}[t]}$ from t1 to t2 (see the
arm-gap parameterisation below). Priors follow the shared template in `priors.py`.
